title: How to get the free LEGO Pokémon Ditto as Squirtle gift with purchase
summary: LEGO Pokémon fans can currently earn a free 40887 Ditto as Squirtle: Movie Night set by spending £115 or more on SMART Play sets, but the offer won't last long.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO is running a limited gift-with-purchase promotion tied to its new Pokémon SMART Play range. Spend £115 / $130 / €130 or more on the newly released SMART Play sets and you'll receive the 40887 Ditto as Squirtle: Movie Night model for free.

The SMART Play line launched on 1 August 2026 and spans twelve sets, from the small £12.99 72159 Jigglypuff Concert up to the £109.99 72167 Charizard vs. Jolteon Ultimate Battle. Several of these sets require a SMART Brick to unlock interactive features, which can be found in sets like 72164 Training House with Pikachu.

According to Brick Fanatics, the Ditto gift is only available until 10 August 2026 or while stocks last, so shoppers hoping to bag it will need to act quickly and combine a few sets to clear the spending threshold.

## Why it matters
Gift-with-purchase promotions are a great way to add exclusive builds to a collection without buying a huge set, and this one has reportedly been well received in early reviews. For UK Pokémon and LEGO fans, it's a chance to pick up a characterful bonus model alongside sets that suit a range of budgets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on stock levels at official LEGO retailers as the 10 August deadline approaches, since the offer could end early if the gift sells out before then.

title: LEGO SMART Play update: Pokémon joins the line-up as tech expands to 21 sets
summary: LEGO's SMART Play technology, which debuted in Star Wars sets earlier this year, has now expanded into LEGO Pokémon, with 21 sets across both themes now confirmed to use the interactive bricks.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's SMART Play technology first launched in March 2026 with a run of LEGO Star Wars sets, including the All-In-One 75421 Darth Vader's TIE Fighter, 75423 Luke's Red Five X-wing, and 75427 Throne Room Duel & A-wing, plus several SMART Play Compatible sets like 75420 Luke's Landspeeder and 75426 Millennium Falcon.

According to Brick Fanatics, the system had a mixed launch, with fans raising concerns over sound quality, design choices, pricing, and the fact the SMART Brick can't be bought separately and isn't included in every set.

As of August 2026, LEGO has officially extended SMART Play beyond Star Wars for the first time, introducing it to LEGO Pokémon with the All-In-One set 72164 Training House with Pikachu. This brings the total number of confirmed SMART Play sets to 21.

## Why it matters
SMART Play expanding into a second theme suggests LEGO Group is committed to developing the technology further rather than shelving it after a rocky start. For collectors and builders, it's worth keeping an eye on which future sets carry the SMART Brick feature, especially since it currently can't be purchased or retrofitted separately - something to factor in before buying.

## What to watch next
It'll be worth watching whether SMART Play spreads to further LEGO themes beyond Star Wars and Pokémon, and whether LEGO addresses ongoing fan feedback around sound design, pricing and separate SMART Brick availability.

title: Fan Builds Darth Maul's Nightmarish Spider Form Using One LEGO Set
summary: A fan designer has recreated Darth Maul's mechanical spider legs from LEGO Star Wars: Terrifying Tales, using only parts from a single official set and instructions available online.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan designer SecondBricks has created a 141-piece build recreating Darth Maul's terrifying spider-legged form, first properly seen in LEGO Star Wars Terrifying Tales. The model uses parts from just one copy of the official 75411 Darth Maul Mech set (£12.99), giving Maul four articulated mechanical legs to crawl and stand on after his defeat by Obi-Wan Kenobi.

Building instructions for the MOC are available via Rebrickable for €1.50, meaning fans can put together this display piece for well under £15 in total. Compared to the smaller spider-Maul version that appeared in Terrifying Tales, this build is bigger and leans further into the spider-like design.

This is a fan-made creation, not an official LEGO Group product, and there's no suggestion the LEGO Group plans to release anything similar.

## Why it matters
It's a neat example of squeezing extra value from a single official set — turning one box into a completely different display model for the price of a coffee's worth of instructions. For Star Wars fans and MOC builders, it's also a reminder that fan designers are often willing to explore darker or more niche character moments that official sets rarely touch.

## What to watch next
Worth keeping an eye on Rebrickable and SecondBricks' other designs for further Darth Maul or Star Wars villain builds using existing official parts.

title: Second Pacific Rim LEGO Ideas Project Qualifies For Review
summary: A giant Gipsy Danger Jaeger build has joined the LEGO Ideas review, meaning Pacific Rim now has two projects in contention for an official set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A new LEGO Ideas submission based on Pacific Rim has hit the 10,000-supporter mark and entered the current review stage, according to Brick Fanatics. Designed by Cosmic.Nomad, the project recreates Gipsy Danger, the Jaeger from the 2013 film, as a hefty 3,334-piece model standing 49cm tall.

The build includes an opening chest for two minifigure pilots, a forearm-mounted sword, a swappable hand, and elbow rockets, plus eight minifigures covering key characters from the movie. This is the second Pacific Rim project to qualify for LEGO Ideas review, bringing the total number of projects under consideration to 64 as part of the second 2026 review wave.

Brick Fanatics notes there's precedent for LEGO combining separate Ideas submissions into one set, pointing to 21343 Viking Village as an example where two designers' projects were merged. That raises the possibility, though it's speculative, that both Pacific Rim entries could be folded together if selected.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is where fan concepts get a genuine shot at becoming retail sets, and a giant robot brick-build has obvious appeal for stadium and large-scale display fans alike. Having two Pacific Rim projects in the same review round shows real community appetite for the franchise, which could strengthen its chances of LEGO Group approval.

## What to watch next
The review window closes in just over a month. It's worth remembering that reaching 10,000 votes only guarantees a project gets considered — it does not confirm LEGO Group will produce it as an official set. Any merger of the two Pacific Rim projects, similar to the Viking Village precedent, remains speculation at this stage.

title: Andrew Garfield surprised by his own $15,000 rare LEGO Spider-Man minifigure
summary: A 2013 San Diego Comic-Con exclusive LEGO minifigure of Andrew Garfield's Spider-Man now fetches around $15,000 on the secondary market, and the actor himself hadn't even seen it until now.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Actor Andrew Garfield, who played Spider-Man in three films between 2012 and 2021, was shown his own ultra-rare LEGO minifigure for the first time in a clip shared by content creator MiniSuperHerosToday. The figure was originally a 2013 San Diego Comic-Con exclusive, limited to just 350 copies and given out via a daily lottery to attendees. These days it typically sells for around $15,000 on the secondary market.

Garfield appeared genuinely unaware that a version of his Spider-Man had ever been made into a LEGO minifigure. Fellow actor Claire Foy, present during the reveal, joked that so few were produced because nobody wanted one.

A more common, mass-produced Andrew Garfield Spider-Man minifigure later appeared in set 76261 Spider-Man Final Battle in 2023, making it far more accessible than the original con-exclusive version.

Meanwhile, current Spider-Man actor Tom Holland has three official LEGO sets tied to Spider-Man: Brand New Day now available: 76346 Spider-Man Hero Figure, 76349 Spider-Man Prison Transport Chase, and 76350 Spider-Man vs. Hulk Epic Clash, priced between £44.99 and £89.99.

## Why it matters
Stories like this highlight just how valuable exclusive convention minifigures can become over time, especially compared to standard retail versions of the same character. For collectors, it's a reminder that limited-run promotional figures often carry far more long-term value than anything found in a regular set.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on secondary marketplaces for any resale activity following renewed interest in this figure, and watch for how LEGO continues supporting the Spider-Man: Brand New Day range with future sets.

title: LEGO Monorail parts now live on Pick a Brick

title: LEGO Monorail parts land on Pick a Brick — here's what a basic track loop costs
summary: LEGO Education's monorail elements are now buyable individually via Pick a Brick in the UK and Europe, reigniting hopes for a full Classic Space monorail comeback. We break down the cost of building a small loop.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's monorail system has quietly resurfaced — not as a retail set, but as individual elements on Pick a Brick, LEGO's pick-and-build parts service. These are officially LEGO Education monorail pieces, including straight and curved white/grey track sections and transparent chassis parts, and they're now listed for UK and European customers (the US listing hasn't gone live yet).

According to Brick Fanatics, a small loop using four curved sections and two straights would cost around £14.22, with an unmotorised chassis adding roughly £2.47 on top. Building three chassis plus that smaller track loop comes to about £16.69 — before factoring in extra pieces for supports or monorail train cars themselves.

Instructions for the LEGO Education monorail system are also available, showing fans how the various elements slot together, including how a longer axle and elastic band can be used to motorise the gear inside the chassis.

## Why it matters
The Classic Space monorail is one of the most nostalgic and requested LEGO Ideas-style revivals among AFOLs, so any sign of parts returning — even via an Education-focused channel — is a big deal for fans hoping for a full retail comeback. For custom builders and stadium/display fans in the Bricks in a Bag community, buyable monorail track and chassis pieces open the door to bespoke transport layouts and diorama additions without needing rare secondhand parts.

## What to watch next
**Rumour:** Whether this points to a full standalone LEGO Monorail retail set in future remains speculation at this stage — nothing has been confirmed beyond the Pick a Brick and LEGO Education listings. Keep an eye on whether the US region gets access to these parts, and whether LEGO expands the monorail range further.

title: LEGO Wednesday theme finally gets its first minifigure
summary: LEGO's Wednesday theme is introducing its first minifigure this October with the new 76788 Nevermore Academy set, following a similar shift seen in LEGO Wicked.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO is adding minifigures to its Wednesday theme for the first time, roughly two years after the range launched. The change arrives with 76788 Nevermore Academy, an 890-piece microscale set priced at £59.99, due in October. It includes a new Wednesday minifigure, whose look borrows from her mini-doll hairstyle and a design that previously appeared in Fortnite.

Until now, Wednesday sets have relied on mini-dolls, mixing playsets and props designed to conceal them. This mirrors how LEGO Wicked also began with mini-dolls only, before introducing minifigures in a couple of 18+ sets in 2025, such as 75685 Emerald City Wall Art and 75691 Glinda & Elphaba Bookends.

According to Brick Fanatics, Wednesday is expected to remain active into 2027, while Wicked appears to have wound down, with no new sets this year and its remaining models set to retire in December.

**Rumour:** Any suggestion of further Wednesday minifigures beyond this one is speculation at this stage, based on how the Wicked theme evolved - nothing else has been confirmed.

## Why it matters
For minifigure collectors, this is a notable shift for a licensed theme that's stuck to mini-dolls since launch. It hints LEGO may be applying lessons from Wicked to other mini-doll-based themes, which could affect how future licensed sets are designed and collected.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on whether Nevermore Academy's minifigure remains a one-off or if more Wednesday characters get the minifigure treatment, and whether LEGO Wicked sees any further sets before its December retirement.

title: LEGO Technic blind boxes reportedly lack scan codes in Australia
summary: Fans in Australia say the new LEGO Technic Mighty Machines blind boxes don't have the usual scannable codes, meaning there's no way to peek at what's inside before buying. It's a rumour for now, sourced from a Reddit report.
bodyMarkdown:

Instead, the base of the box reportedly only has the standard barcode found on all LEGO products.

Each Mighty Machines box contains one of eight tiny Technic models at random, and in most regions a scannable code lets curious buyers (or scalpers) check the contents before opening. If this report is accurate, Australian shoppers won't have that option and will have to buy blind, as LEGO presumably intended.

This isn't the first time fans in Australia have had a rougher deal with blind-box products - Collectible Minifigures series typically launch a month later there than elsewhere.

**This is currently a rumour**, based on a single Reddit report rather than any official LEGO statement, so treat it as unconfirmed until more buyers or retailers weigh in.

Scannable codes have become a handy (if slightly against-the-spirit-of-blind-boxes) tool for collectors wanting specific figures or models without opening multiple boxes. If LEGO is quietly removing them in some markets, it could signal a wider rollback - bad news for collectors who rely on scanning to track down exact pieces, and a change worth watching if you build or collect Technic or Minifigures lines.

title: Rumour: LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit set may stay close to its original size

If the rumoured 1,038-piece figure is accurate, that means the finished set may have grown by just 38 pieces or so from the original pitch — a notably small change compared with other recent LEGO Ideas buildable figures.

For comparison, 21372 La Catrina reportedly shrank to roughly half its original size, 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial dropped from a huge 2,990-element fan design down to 1,226 pieces in the final set, and 21361 Gremlins: Gizmo actually grew from 400 elements to 1,125 pieces. Wallace & Gromit, by contrast, looks set to stay much truer to its original scale — though small tweaks within the rumoured piece count are still possible.

Importantly, LEGO has not officially announced the Wallace & Gromit Ideas set at all yet, so all of the above remains unconfirmed.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas fans often see big differences between a winning fan design and the final retail set, in both size and price. If this rumour holds up, it suggests LEGO is aiming to preserve the spirit and scale of Pidelium's original Wallace & Gromit concept — good news for fans who backed the project hoping for a faithful adaptation, and a useful data point for anyone trying to predict pricing and piece counts on future Ideas sets.
